blocks.x: Starting October 17, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will officially land on Netflix for audiences in the United States. The timing is worth noting because Crunchyroll is still handling the same-day rollout in Japan and other regions, with the enhanced series premiering on October 11. Netflix is taking the slower route, putting the episodes out one week after their Japanese broadcast rather than going head-to-head with the simulcast.

Netflix is also treating Beerus as more than a one-off U.S. release. The upcoming schedule lists the series for several international territories as well, giving Dragon Ball Super: Beerus a much wider streaming reach. Viewers who want to watch Goku's remastered battles against Beerus as soon as possible will still have to look elsewhere, though.

For everyone else, a one-week wait isn't exactly the end of the world. This isn't a new Dragon Ball story where missing the first episode could mean getting spoiled before breakfast. Beerus is revisiting material from the original Dragon Ball Super run, now with Toei going back over the early episodes and rebuilding them for this new version. For viewers who don't want another streaming subscription just to watch Goku fight the God of Destruction a few days earlier, Netflix's schedule is a pretty easy trade-off.

blocks.x: The bigger question now is just how far Netflix's deal with Dragon Ball Super: Beerus actually goes. While Netflix has the U.S. release listed for October 17, the full details of the streaming rights still aren't completely clear. Dragon Ball’s absence from Crunchyroll's current Fall 2026 lineup only makes things more interesting, especially after the platform handled Dragon Ball Daima's rollout and English dub.

If Netflix does end up being the main U.S. streaming home for Beerus, American fans will have to get used to the one-week delay. The Japanese broadcast begins October 11, while Netflix's first batch arrives on October 17. That means six days of dodging spoilers every time Goku, Vegeta, or Beerus starts trending online.

This is the same Beerus story that has already been watched countless times, now rebuilt with new cuts, re-rendered footage, and updated sound and music. If Netflix really is becoming part of Dragon Ball's next TV era, watching Goku meet the God of Destruction again might just be the start.
